title: Variables
description: How to store a value and give it a name so you can use it later.

content.value: A variable is a way to store a value and give it a name, like a labeled box. To make one, write the name you want, an equals sign `=`, then the value. Now the name and the value are linked: whenever you use the name, Python gives you back the value.
Names can have letters, digits and underscores, but they can't start with a digit or have spaces. `player_score` works; `2ndScore` and `player score` do not.
A variable can hold a new value later. When you write `score = 250`, Python throws away the old value and stores the new one. The name stays the same; only the value inside the box changes.

practice.question: Make a variable named 'age', store your age in it (like 10 or 12), and print it.

quiz.question: What is a variable?
options: A named place to store a value.
A secret code to hack games.
quiz.explain: A variable is a name that stores a value, so the computer can remember it and use it later.

quiz.question: How do you store the number 5 in a variable named 'apples'?
quiz.explain: The name goes on the left and the value goes on the right: `apples = 5`. You can't put the number on the left of the `=`.
